title: WPSS/2247/2014 of Santosh Kumar Pal Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2247 of 2014
Santosh Kumar Pal Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. S.S. Yadav, Advocate, present for the petitioner
Mr. Vikas Pandey, Brief Holder, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner is a Senior-Eye-Assistant in the
Community Centre, Luksar, Haridwar. By an order dated
14.08.2014 he was transferred from Haridwar to Champawat
and the said order was challenged by the petitioner before
this Court in a petition being WPSS No. 1273 of 2014, which
was disposed vide order dated 27.08.2014 directing that the
petitioner shall join his services at his transferred place and
then made a representation to the Director General, Medical
Health & Family Welfare, Dehradun. Aggrieved by the said
order, the petitioner filed a Special Appeal before this Court,
which was dismissed vide order dated 17.09.2014. Though
the appeal was dismissed but the impugned order, passed
by this Court, slightly modified to the extent that the
condition imposed on the petitioner to join at transferred
place i.e. Champawat was relaxed.
2. Thereafter, the petitioner filed a representation
before the Director General, Medical Health & Family
Welfare, Dehradun, who after considering the entire report
and available material, rejected the representation of the
petitioner. The finding is that the petitioner has been
working at ìLuksarî Haridwar since 18.05.2005. His
transfer was long due. Before the transfer he had given
three choices i.e. Dehradun, Udham Singh Nagar and
Nainital, but as in all these three places the post of Senior-Eye-Assistant is not available he cannot be transferred to

2
these places. The only place vacant was at Champawat.
There is hence no scope for changing the transfer order
dated 18.10.2014 says the authorities and hence his
representation has been rejected.
3. No relief, therefore, can be granted to the
petitioner, now as the concerned authority have assigned
their reasons for transferring the petitioner to Champawat.
The writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed. This Court
has been informed that the petitioner has not joined his
duties at Champawat since August 2014. It is hence made
clear that in case the petitioner does not join his duties at
Champawat immediately, the Department concerned shall
be at liberty to initiate disciplinary proceedings against the
petitioner.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
17.03.2015
Aswal/Nitesh
